row_object: Emmitsburg Road fences (Intact -> Splintered / breached; attackers climbing)
fence_state_at_battle_start: PDF: "Intact morning Jul 3" and double post-and-rail on both sides. OR primary evidence: post-and-rail fences did stand across the Confederate route on Jul 3 (Peyton, Shepard) but segments near the Union right-of-centre had been pulled down and used for breastworks on Jul 2 (Gibbon, Harrow, Hancock, Joslin) and Third Corps fence-clearing took place on the morning of Jul 2 (Meade, Humphreys, Higgins, Bodine). So the single state "Intact" at morning Jul 3 is a simplification contradicted in part.
documented_damage_or_removal: Jul 3: fences climbed and slowed the advance (Peyton, Shepard). Damage by fire on Jul 2-3 is stated in the PDF (Savas-Hessler) and was not verified. No breach point documented.
verdict: conflict (Intact vs Jul 2 pull-downs); slowing supported; 836 holes and double fences unverified
tier: documented (fences existed and obstructed on Jul 3; segment pull-downs on Jul 2); inferred (breaches, extent of Jul 2 removal); gap (836 holes)
source_citation: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.2: Peyton (OR27-2-R441) p.386; Shepard (R552) pp.646-647. pt.1: Gibbon (R098) p.416; Harrow (R099) p.419; Hancock (R076) p.370; Joslin (R101) p.423; Meade (R006) p.131; Humphreys (R158) p.532; Higgins (R146) p.511; Bodine (R167) p.556
supporting_passage_ref: See subclaims; each quote verified by tools/bt/or27_find.py --verify (exact phrase located in the OR27 OCR text, this session).
structures_tie_in: state_schedule S-062; structures FEN-emmitsburg-road (state_changes row S-062), P-10 (pre-existing Peach Orchard/Wheatfield/Emmitsburg Rd fences), FEN-sherfy-orchard. Suggestion: carry "segments pulled down Jul 2" as a selectable state, no default (Law cl.6).
notes: Wright (OR27-2-R539) p.623 also shows 'post and rail fences' crossed on Jul 2 by Anderson's division; that is another sector.

subclaims.claim: post-and-rail fences existed across the Confederate advance on Jul 3 and had to be climbed
subclaims.cite: Peyton (OR27-2-R441) p.386: "climb three high post and rail fences", the last one "behind the last of which the enemy's skirmishers were first met"; verified by tools/bt/or27_find.py --verify (exact phrase located in the OR27 OCR text, this session)

subclaims.claim: a lane enclosed by two post-and-plank fences about 180-200 yards from the Union works obstructed Archer's-sector troops
subclaims.cite: Shepard (OR27-2-R552) p.647: "a lane inclosed by two stout post and" [OCR: jjlank] "fences", "a very great obstruction"; phrase located by --verify; the word plank is read from the NPS Gettysburg web transcription seen in a search summary (page not opened). Shepard's OCR reads "ISO or 200 yards"; 180 is the NPS-transcription reading. This is a lane with two fences, which may or may not be the Emmitsburg Road.

subclaims.claim: "Intact morning Jul 3" along the whole road
subclaims.cite: Fences were pulled down on Jul 2 along the Emmitsburg road near a "brick house": Gibbon (OR27-1-R098) p.416 "tore down the fences and constructed breastworks"; Harrow (R099) p.419 "hastily taken down and piled in their front"; Hancock (R076) p.370 "slight breastwork of such materials as the adjoining fences afforded"; Joslin (R101) p.423 "small breastwork of rails behind the fence". Third Corps fronts: Meade (R006) p.131 Sickles "leveling all the fences and stone walls"; Humphreys (R158) p.532 "removing such of the fences as were in the way"; Higgins (R146) p.511 order to "demolish all stone walls and fences in our front to the Emmitsburg road"; Bodine (R167) p.556 detailed "to clear away the fences in front of the division". All verified by tools/bt/or27_find.py --verify (exact phrase located in the OR27 OCR text, this session). Which segments are meant, and whether the brick house is the Codori house, is not established.
